title: Poor Pitch Condition in Ponte Preta vs. CRB Match Draws Attention
seoTitle: Ponte Preta Pitch Condition Draws Attention in Serie B
subtitle: Pitch condition at Moisés Lucarelli Stadium reflects Ponte Preta's financial crisis
excerpt: The pitch at Moisés Lucarelli Stadium came under scrutiny after Ponte Preta's win over CRB, highlighting the club's deep financial crisis.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
In Round 29 of Série B, Ponte Preta's 1-0 victory over CRB brought to light the precarious condition of the pitch at Moisés Lucarelli Stadium in Campinas. The poor state of the field has drawn attention due to its direct link to the crisis gripping the club.

Pitch condition during the match

Released photos show nutsedge, a type of weed, in several areas of the field. The images reveal worn patches that hinder the normal flow of the match.

Cause of pitch deterioration

A lack of regular maintenance is cited as the primary reason for the pitch's poor condition. The club has been unable to cover the costs required for the stadium's proper upkeep.

Ponte Preta's financial crisis

The near-insolvency scenario, mentioned by legal director José Henrique Specie, reflects recurring wage delays since 2025. Players, football staff, and club employees report going up to six months without pay, with some cases nearing a full year.

Recent board measures

Recently, the board settled one month of overdue wages for academy players who are part of the senior squad and part of a month for other players. One month's salary was also paid to staff, although significant arrears remain.

Club members' reaction

At the latest Extraordinary General Meeting, club members rejected the creation of a Football Corporation (SAF), blocking the approval which required a two-thirds majority of those present.

Impact on the Série B standings

With the victory over CRB, Ponte Preta reached 13 points, still far from escaping the relegation zone, where 19 points are needed to climb out of last place. The club remains virtually relegated to Série C in 2027.

With information from ge.
